is a necessary truth, as is . For some suitable p and q, [p∧q] is merely partially grounded in [p], despite the fact that is true in all possible worlds. Moral: the distinction between full and mere partial grounding is an explanatory distinction rather than a purely modal one.
overview: This passage rejects a shortcut argument from modal entailment to full grounding. It matters because the paper’s positive argument cannot simply define full grounding by modal entailment; it must explain why full grounding necessitates without collapsing grounding into modality. The example uses necessary truths to show that entailment can accompany partial grounding trivially.
title: Modal Distinction Problem
